boundaries: microphone MediaStream -> AudioWorklet (render thread) -> page (message port)
page -> call socket -> Go relay (16 kHz PCM binary frames)
Go relay -> call socket -> page (24 kHz PCM binary frames, JSON events)

instruments.evidence: Phase 3a: a capture worklet served from public/, the PCM conversion, chunker and player, and the call socket client, with their tests. Nothing on screen uses them yet; Phase 3b wires them into the call modal.

Read the call-audio findings of five ledgers. R8 (a dropped notice stalled every later sentence) cannot recur: each binary frame is played on its own and nothing waits on a notice. R4 (video spoke twice) is untouched, since video mode is not changed. The WebKit lesson in callRecorder -- keep a JavaScript reference to the source node or it is collected and reads silence -- is kept: the capture's stop() closes over the source, the worklet node and the gain.

Printed the socket URL for two bases that differ on what the builder branches on: http with a path gives ws://localhost:8080/api/v1/omnichat/calls/call-1/live?token=tok; https with a trailing slash and a query gives wss://.../api/v1/omnichat/calls/a%2Fb/live?token=t, the base's query dropped and the id escaped.

The four event types the client accepts are spelled as the Go constants LiveCallEventHeard, Said, Interrupted and TurnComplete; the capture processor name matches between the worklet's registerProcessor and the AudioWorkletNode.

The relay writes audio as binary frames and events as JSON with type and text; the client routes ArrayBuffer to audio and parses strings as events, requiring text for heard and said, which the relay only sends non-empty.

instruments.why: No rule lives in two places.

instruments.evidence: The relay expects 16 kHz mono PCM and reads frames up to 64 KB; a chunk is 3,200 bytes. Live answers in 24 kHz mono PCM, which is the rate the player tags its buffers with.

instruments.why: No field added to a struct.

instruments.evidence: The chunker's output was read back through a real browser's audio graph rather than trusted from the unit test's arrays; see B5.

The unit tests feed the chunker 128-sample frames, the size a real worklet render quantum delivers, and the player's fake context mirrors createBuffer's duration arithmetic; the real browser run confirms both.
48 kHz and 44.1 kHz input both produce exactly 1,600 samples per 100 ms; the real browser ran at 44.1 kHz.
Unknown event types, a heard event without text, and non-JSON are ignored; an odd trailing byte of audio is dropped rather than misread.
Samples beyond full scale clip to 32767 and -32768 rather than wrapping; an empty chunk plays nothing; a frame larger than the chunker's buffer grows it.

Against openMicrophone: the same zero-gain route to the destination keeps the graph pulled, and the context is the caller's, already resumed during the click that started the call, which is what Safari requires.
Every branch of the socket client -- open, refused before open, audio, event, unknown event, dropped send when closed or backed up -- is reached by a test.
A refusal before open rejects with a message; a close after open is reported with its code and reason, so the caller can say why the call ended.
The socket URL follows the /ws construction but for a different path; the token fetch is the same endpoint. Nothing duplicated beyond the one URL rule each owns.

Suspected that loading the capture module twice on one context would reject a second registerProcessor and break a capture restarted on the same context; the real browser accepted a second capture on the same context. Not a finding.
The only cross-thread traffic is the worklet's message port, which copies each batch; the page's state is touched on one thread.
stop() disconnects every node it made and detaches the port handler; clear() stops and disconnects every scheduled source.

instruments.why: No finding, so no fix to control.

instruments.evidence: tsc -b exit 0 and eslint exit 0 on the five files, both exit codes captured directly this time rather than through a pipe; the 18 new tests pass. The full suite has not been run.

Ran the real module in a real browser page (the Vite dev server, a 44.1 kHz AudioContext) with a 440 Hz tone at half scale through a real MediaStream: 9 chunks in about a second, every one 3,200 bytes; peak 16,375 against the ideal 16,384; 88 zero crossings per 100 ms, which is exactly 440 Hz, so the rate conversion keeps pitch; the real player reported playing after enqueue and stopped after clear, signalling [true, false]. Unverified and recorded as such: whether the browser's echo cancellation removes her voice from the microphone when it is played through Web Audio on speakers. A headless page has neither, so it is a Phase 3b test on a real machine with speakers, not a pass here.

instruments.why: Nothing is started ahead of a decision.
